name: sol_ec_6
description: External call with hardcoded fixed gas amount causing out-of-gas failure/DoS
question: The source file in `source` performs an external call (e.g. call{gas: <fixed_value>}(...) or .call{gas: <fixed_value>}) using a hardcoded, fixed gas stipend rather than forwarding all available gas or a dynamically computed amount, such that the call can run out of gas and revert or fail unexpectedly (e.g. due to future gas cost changes or a callee consuming more gas), causing denial of service or fund lock, excluding cases where the fixed low gas amount is intentionally used to limit gas to a trusted or simple recipient (e.g. 2300 gas transfer to prevent reentrancy) and any failure is properly handled or non-critical.
criteria: A payment/refund loop iterates over multiple recipients using call{gas: 30000}(...) or similar fixed value, where a single recipient's failure or increased gas cost can halt distribution to all others
A fee/reward transfer to an externally-controlled or arbitrary address uses .call{value: amount, gas: fixedAmount}("") with a hardcoded gas number, without fallback or gas re-estimation
A critical state-changing external call specifies a fixed gas cap (e.g. gas: 21000, gas: 50000) that does not account for callee logic complexity, causing reverts when the callee needs more gas
Code sends ETH/tokens via a low-level call with a static gas value and no retry/fallback mechanism if the call fails due to insufficient gas
